newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends slightly down vs US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends slightly down vs US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed slightly down at 8.2944 on Friday against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on a technical correction from its two-month high of 8.2942 on Thursday, traders said.
The weighted average price on Thursday was 8.2948.
Dealers said a correction was expected after the yuan had hit two-month highs for two days in a row.

The yuan opened down at an intraday low of 8.2948 and then rose steadily to move in the range of 8.2940 and 8.2945 for most of the session, hitting a high of 8.2895. Trading was dull with most business done at about 8.2944, traders said.

One dealer said pro-yuan sentiment was still strong despite Friday's fall. "The yuan moved at a high level between 8.2940 and 8.2950 for most of the session, backed by strong pro-yuan sentiment," he said.
A second dealer said the yuan was likely to stand firmly above the key 8.2950 level after having closed above that level for several days in a row.
"The yuan's upward trend will continue in the short term unless the central bank intervenes resolutely," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move above the 8.2950 level early next week.
The yuan closed little changed at 6.5625 from 6.5615 against 100 Japanese yen and up at an intraday high of 1.0700 from 1.0710 against the Hong Kong dollar.
